open.heading:
Curious today.
{{Confident tomorrow.}}
body: Five classes, and five published syllabus documents. The curriculum is CBSE’s, and the school issues it class by class as its **PRECEPT** syllabus — a separate document for every year from Nursery to Class XII, for session **2026-27**. Primary is five of them.

Alongside the timetable, Classes III to V take **Impetus** — the school’s own activity programme, and the reason a nine-year-old here ends up on a stage with a microphone explaining where she finds mathematics.
The four are the school’s own, published on {' '}Teaching & Learning as what every class is taught against.

rail.heading:
One class teacher.
{{Four specialists.}}
body: The school advertises its primary posts by name, and the shape of the stage is in the wording: one **mother teacher** carrying every subject, with dance, storytelling and music taught by people hired to teach only that.

**On subjects.** The school publishes that a PRECEPT syllabus document exists for every class. It does not publish what is inside one, so no primary subject scheme is set out here — only the posts and rooms it names itself. See {' '}Curriculum.

appr.heading:
Think. Explore.
{{Understand.}}
body: The school states four commitments and measures an ordinary Tuesday morning against them. They are quoted below in its own words rather than paraphrased.

act.heading:
Learning doesn’t stop
{{at the desk.}}
body: The clearest thing about this stage is not a description of it — it is the record. Every line below names the class that did it, and each is something the school published rather than something claimed on its behalf.
The full record, year group by year group, is on {' '}Student Success.

val.heading:
Good habits.
{{Strong character.}}
body: Three words, read off the crest on the school gate — and the school’s own gloss on each.

space.heading:
Spaces that
{{inspire learning.}}
body: A primary child at Sunbeam does not spend the week in one room. The rooms below are the school’s own published inventory, and the junior computer laboratory is sized so a nine-year-old works alone rather than in a group of four.
Every room above is listed on the school’s own {' '}facilities inventory.

close.heading:
Strong today.
{{Ready for tomorrow.}}
body: Five classes, five published syllabus documents, one activity programme of the school’s own — and a record of what each year group entered and brought home. Subject lists, period allocations and the contents of the PRECEPT documents are not published, and are not estimated here.
